conventions.convention: The positive in-plane normal n to the oriented over-tangent t satisfies that (t,n) is positively oriented. It points from the source underarc to the target underarc, whose color is source * over.
Right translation is R_y(x)=x*y; right division is R_y inverse applied to x. Quandles additionally satisfy x*x=x. Empty underlying sets are not excluded.
Adjoint generators satisfy e_(q*r)=e_r inverse · e_q · e_r, matching the positive-meridian Wirtinger relation g_v=g_o inverse · g_u · g_o.
Fox computations use an odd prime p, operation a*b=2b−a, and one variable per maximal underarc. Repeated arc coefficients are added. Zero free variables produce the empty tuple once.
Finite-table inputs have m≥1; rows index the first operand and columns index the second. Rack mode checks column permutations and right self-distributivity; quandle mode also checks the diagonal.

Local coloring calculations are choice-free; ACω is assumed for ambient-isotopy conclusions and the smooth framing interpretation. Positive curls transport labels by the kink map and negative curls by its inverse.

load_bearing.statement: A quandle has idempotency, bijective right translations, and right self-distributivity. Diagram colorings satisfy d=a*b for source, over, and target colors a,b,d.

Every oriented Reidemeister move and planar isotopy induces a canonical bijection between quandle coloring sets. Under ACω, diagrams of ambient-isotopic oriented links have bijective coloring sets. The stated local unique-extension property conversely forces the quandle axioms.
Defines racks, their positive-normal diagram colorings, the diagram quandle as a quotient of finite terms by quandle and crossing identities, and the adjoint group by conjugation relators.

For every odd prime p and every finite regular oriented link diagram D, the Fox algorithm terminates and returns exactly Col_p(D). With f free variables it returns p^f colorings, with the stated pivot-search and row-operation bounds.
Let R be a rack, with right translations R_y(x)=x*y. The kink map π(x)=x*x is a bijection. Its inverse is π inverse(z)=R_z inverse(z).

Assume ACω. Diagram quandles of any two regular oriented diagrams of a nonempty oriented link are isomorphic. For a one-component link K, Adj(Q(D)) is isomorphic to the stated positive-meridian Wirtinger group W(D) and to π₁(S³ minus K).

The full orientation and height-order variants of local R1, R2, and R3 moves.
Under ACω, ambient-isotopic oriented links have diagrams related by finitely many planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves.
The precise ACω hypothesis retained in ambient-isotopy and smooth-framing conclusions.
Smooth oriented links in the standard oriented three-sphere and orientation-preserving ambient equivalence.
